Subject: Priority gating matrix & acceptance runway — MedVanta MAP

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. Procurement/legal here have asked for a short mutual action plan that lays out: (1) evaluation checkpoints and success criteria for our pilot, (2) sequencing for MSA / DPA / order form so we know what to prioritize, and (3) proposed target dates for procurement sign-off.

High-level ask from our side: we want to be ready to go live (production traffic) by early October if the pilot works — but that depends on how quickly we can resolve the DPA redlines. Can you send a MAP with explicit owners (both sides), and a recommended sequencing? Also, we'll need an evidence bundle (SOC2/pen test) for legal.

Attaching: none yet — please send your MAP.

Regards,
Alex

Sr. Manager, Procurement
MedVanta Health

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Priority gating matrix & acceptance runway — MedVanta MAP

Alex — thanks, and totally doable. I attached a concise MAP (MAP-PriorityMatrix-v1.xlsx) that splits the plan into three lanes: Eval (PoC), Legal/Procurement, and Ops/Onboarding. Key points up front:

- Recommended sequencing (high level):
  1) Finalize MSA baseline (commercial terms) — parallel path for DPA redlines to speed cycle.
  2) Resolve DPA security/processing clauses — necessary before order form countersignature if data residency / processing terms change.
  3) Order form executed after DPA agreed (otherwise billing/KMS/evidence gating remains open).

- Proposed timeline (draft):
  * Eval run: 2026-09-20 -> 2026-10-02 (two-week performance + functional test window).
  * DPA redline round 1 review (MedVanta legal): complete by 2026-09-17.
  * Legal sign-off window: target 2026-09-24.
  * Order form signature target: 2026-10-01.
  * Canary / limited production: 2026-10-05 -> 2026-10-19 (14-day acceptance window).

- Dependencies called out in the MAP: MSA signature (for commercial terms), DPA acceptance (for data processing and evidence), order form (commit capacity + billing), SOC2 report + access to audit logs (evidence).

Action items (please confirm owners on your side):
- Who is MedVanta legal lead for DPA redlines?
- Confirm procurement target date to complete commercial review.

I've looped in Laura (legal) and Karthik (contracts) for sequencing and Neha for the Eval plan. Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk the MAP.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Alex / Jasmine — quick legal note on sequencing:

- We can run the MSA (commercial) and DPA redline exchange in parallel, but operationally we should avoid executing the order form until the DPA's core security and processing obligations are agreed. If the DPA introduces material processing constraints, it can impact billing (e.g., on-prem vs hosted) and key management (KMS) choices.

- Proposed legal cadence:
  * MedVanta sends initial DPA comments by 2026-09-17.
  * Redwood returns consolidated positions and a redline mapping by 2026-09-20.
  * Final negotiations aim to complete by 2026-09-24.

- Evidence: please request the SOC2 Type II report and our pen-test summary. Those will be posted to the evidence link in the MAP. We can also provide subprocessor list and data-flow diagram on request.

I've attached DPA_redlines_v3.pdf with our proposed compromises to the data transfer and retention sections — these are flagged in the mapping sheet. For anything that materially changes the architecture (e.g., full on-prem requirement), we need to re-open commercial terms.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_redlines_v3.pdf]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, jasmine.liu@redwood.com, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@medvanta.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority gating matrix & acceptance runway — MedVanta MAP

Adding sequencing recommendations and a fallback plan:

- Sequencing we recommend (detailed):
  1) Sign MSA baseline to lock commercial terms (pricing bands and termination).
  2) Exchange and close DPA redlines in parallel; log remaining open items in a short exception schedule if needed.
  3) Execute order form only once DPA open items are resolved or captured in the exception schedule (order form requires clear data processing terms).

- Acceptance gating + rollback drivers:
  * Canary duration: 14 days (as Jasmine suggested). Pass = meet functional + performance SLAs and no critical security findings.
  * Rollback drivers during canary: sustained error rate >1.5% or sustained 95th latency above agreed threshold for more than 6 hours.

- Docs attached: redline-mapping.csv (maps each DPA clause to proposed language and owner).

If MedVanta is comfortable with us tracking any low-risk open items in an exceptions schedule (attached to the order form), we can keep the target order form signature date while continuing to resolve minor DPA clarifications. That avoids holdups where legal needs minor clarifications but procurement wants to commit capacity.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redline-mapping.csv]

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Priority gating matrix & acceptance runway — MedVanta MAP

Alex — to make the Eval lane concrete, here's the acceptance plan we'll run during the two-week pilot window (2026-09-20 -> 2026-10-02):

- Functional checkpoints:
  1) Feature coverage smoke tests (day 1) — sample prompts validated against baseline responses.
  2) Latency and throughput baseline (day 1-3) — measure 50th/95th/99th pct latencies under expected concurrency.
  3) Semantic quality checks (day 4-10) — Q&A/summary evaluation on a curated prompt set.
  4) Regression and hallucination spot checks (ongoing).

- Success criteria (pass/fail):
  * Functional: >= 95% case pass on smoke tests.
  * Performance: 95th latency <= 700ms for the expected concurrency profile.
  * Quality: average model score >= 4.0/5 across the curated prompt set; incident rate for hallucinations <= 2%.

- Evidence deliverables to Redwood/MedVanta: test logs, sample transcripts, token-level cost estimates, and a short summary report within 3 business days of test completion. We'll need a temporary API key and a sandbox dataset (non-PII) from MedVanta for run-by-run validation.

I'll coordinate schedule availability with your engineering lead — who should I invite for API credentials setup?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
